sections.h2: Where are the Mason County tax offices in Maysville?
sections.html:
All three offices are in Maysville. One values the property, one collects the current bill, and one records deeds and inherits whatever stays unpaid.

  • PVA: 220 1/2 Sutton Street, (606) 564-3700, open weekdays from half past eight. It handles value, mailing and property addresses, and exemptions.
  • Sheriff: 120 West Third Street, in the old Health Department building, 606-564-3309, open from nine in the morning on weekdays. A drop box takes check payments only.
  • Clerk: 27 West 3rd Street, PO Box 234, (606) 564-3341, opening at eight on weekdays and closing for lunch between 11:30 and 12:30.

One fact helps when a bill looks high: the PVA's page says the office writes no laws and sets no rates. Rates are voted by the fiscal court, by city officials and by school boards, so a complaint about the rate belongs with them, not with the PVA.

sections.h2: What is Mason County like for a seller on the Ohio River?
sections.html:
Mason County is a river county in northeastern Kentucky, and the Ohio River marks its northern edge, facing Brown and Adams counties in Ohio. It was created in 1788 from Bourbon County, Virginia, and honors George Mason, a delegate to the Constitutional Convention. It covers 246 square miles, 240 of them land, and adjoins Lewis, Fleming, Robertson and Bracken counties.

Maysville is the seat and biggest city. The smaller cities are Dover, Germantown and Sardis, and Mays Lick is a census-designated place. Helena, Lewisburg, Minerva, Old Washington, Orangeburg and Shannon are unincorporated. The Census Bureau treats the county as the Maysville micropolitan area, part of the Cincinnati-Wilmington-Maysville combined statistical area.

Mason County was once far larger in people than it is now. The 1800 census counted 12,182, the 1850 census 18,344 and the 1890 census 20,773. The count then fell to 16,666 in 1990, recovered to 17,490 in 2010, and slipped to 17,120 in 2020. The 2025 estimate is 16,936, down 1.1 percent from the 2020 base.

One district, Mason County Schools, runs the public schools. Its campuses are Mason County High School, Mason County Middle School, Mason County Intermediate School and Straub Elementary School.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Mason County homes and work?
sections.html:
Two of every three homes are lived in by their owners, and the population has been shrinking slowly.

The typical household takes in $52,178 and per capita income is $31,189. Poverty is 15.2 percent. Among residents under 65, 18.5 percent report a disability. Adults with a high school diploma number 86.3 percent, and 20.0 percent hold a bachelor's degree. Workers spend 26.8 minutes getting to their jobs. About 908 residents are veterans, and 1,209 businesses have no employees. Employers numbered 404 establishments in 2023, with 6,951 employees and a payroll of $336.4 million, and employment rose 4.9 percent. Health care and social assistance receipts reached $152.4 million in 2022, transportation and warehousing $114.2 million, and retail sales $477.4 million, which is $28,246 per resident.

sections.h2: What does the sheriff's Taxpayer's Notice say about timing and penalties?
sections.html:
The sheriff's notice sets out four periods, and the bill itself arrives on a yellow postcard.

  • Discount of two percent: October 1 through November 1.
  • Face amount: November 2 through December 31.
  • Five percent penalty: all of January.
  • Twenty-one percent penalty: February through April 15.

The ordinary calendar is found in KRS 134.015. When business closes on April 15, unpaid real estate bills move to the County Clerk. From then on, the sheriff says, a 20 percent County Attorney fee, a 10 percent clerk fee and monthly interest of 1 percent attach, and an investor may buy the delinquency. Anything from a prior year is paid at the clerk's counter, and the sheriff gives 606-564-3341 for the figure.

The sheriff mails no past-due reminders. A bounced check costs $50 and puts the bill back to unpaid. Cards work through the online link with a surcharge. If escrow or a new owner is responsible, pass the notice along at once.

sections.h2: How does a Mason County owner appeal a value through the Board of Appeals?
sections.html:
The City of Maysville's board page says appeals run through the PVA: discuss the value with the office, review how it was reached, and appeal to the Board of Appeals if no resolution comes. The city has an appointee on that board, and its page lists the PVA's phone, (606) 564-3700, as the contact.

The PVA's own page adds that staff visit every property at least once in four years and may measure a building's exterior even if nobody is home. In the statute, KRS 133.120 sets the order of steps, and KRS 133.030 puts the board's first meeting 25 to 35 days after inspection closes. Bring evidence of value and keep paying on your claimed figure until the board rules. Anyone you pay to speak for you must come from the statute's list of professionals.

sections.h2: What is the Mason County homestead exemption for 2026?
sections.html: It is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, and it reduces a $161,500 home, the county median, to a taxable $112,400. The owner must live in the house and be 65 or older, or totally disabled. The county website sends applicants to the PVA page, which also hosts a property search and a vehicle-tax exoneration affidavit. Once an age claim is approved it normally stays in place for as long as the same owner lives there. A buyer files a new one.

sections.h2: What should a Mason County seller do about the lien and the deed?
sections.html:
Get this year's balance from the sheriff and earlier years from the clerk, then pay both from the sale proceeds. A delinquency lien may last up to eleven years under KRS 134.015(5) whoever owns the parcel, which is why title agents require payoff.

The deed goes to the clerk at 27 West 3rd Street. The grantor's transfer tax is fifty cents per $500 of value under KRS 142.050, or $161.50 on a sale at the county median. The clerk's contact page names four e-recording services: Hopdox, CSC, Simplifile and ePN. Confirm what each deed needs before sending it.

faqs.q: What are the Mason County Sheriff's office hours?
faqs.a: Nine in the morning to half past four on weekdays, at 120 West Third Street, Maysville. Call 606-564-3309. A drop box takes checks only.

faqs.q: What does a bounced check cost on a Mason County tax bill?
faqs.a: $50. The bill returns to unpaid status, and your repayment should follow the payment period printed on it.

faqs.q: Does the Mason County Sheriff mail past-due notices?
faqs.a: No. None will be mailed, so watch the dates yourself. Real estate bills still open after April 15 go to the County Clerk with added fees.

faqs.q: Who sets tax rates in Mason County?
faqs.a: Elected bodies do: the fiscal court, city officials and school boards, among other taxing authorities. The PVA neither sets rates nor decides the total to be raised.

faqs.q: Can a Mason County bill be paid by card?
faqs.a: Yes, using the online link on the sheriff's site, with an added charge from the card company. Paying in person, by mail or in the check-only drop box also works.
